key_insight: CEDAR, an evidence-citing and self-auditing LLM pipeline, outperformed trained machine learning for pediatric diabetes outcome prediction, with the largest gains on sparsely screened outcomes.
engineering_relevance: Evidence-linked predictions and automated self-auditing offer a design pattern for traceable clinical AI using multimodal medical records.
method: Combined structured records with note-derived social determinants and, for type 1 diabetes, continuous glucose monitoring data.
Used 18 months of follow-up to predict outcomes at 24 months.
Cited chart evidence and self-audited predictions for clinician review.
evidence_signal: Across 2,489 youth with type 2 and 4,018 with type 1 diabetes, pooled AUROC was 0.815 and 0.756 versus ML baselines of 0.656–0.700 and 0.603–0.631, respectively; only 4 of 70,246 cited values mismatched the chart.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish external or prospective validation, so clinical deployment requires testing generalizability and real-world safety.
paper_title: Agentic LLM reasoning in pediatric diabetes outcome prediction from multimodal medical records
